question: How can astronomers measure the spin of a black hole whose horizon they cannot see?
answer: By finding where its gas disc ends. Around a non-spinning hole no orbit is stable inside three horizon radii, so the disc stops there; around a fast spinner the edge closes in almost to the horizon. X-rays from iron in the innermost gas, smeared by gravity and speed, show how close it gets.
move: When the thing itself hides, measure where its surroundings stop behaving.
reference: Tanaka et al., Gravitationally redshifted emission implying an accretion disk and massive black hole in the active galaxy MCG-6-30-15, Nature, 1995
